Nationwide Protests Disrupt Chilean Economy; Sigdo Koppers SA Cites Operational Challenges

SANTIAGO, June 14 — Widespread protests and road blockades continued across Chile on Friday, paralyzing transportation networks and disrupting economic activity throughout the country. The unrest, sparked by proposed constitutional reforms and rising living costs, has entered its fifth day and shows no sign of abating.

Major highways linking key mining and industrial zones remain obstructed, causing delays in shipments and impeding the movement of workers. Port activity in Valparaíso and Antofagasta is reportedly operating at reduced capacity due to labor stoppages and limited access. The Confederation of Production and Commerce of Chile estimates daily losses to the economy at nearly $120 million.

Sigdo Koppers SA, a major industrial conglomerate, reported significant operational challenges as a result of the ongoing crisis. “Our logistics have been severely affected by road closures, and several of our sites are operating with minimal staff,” said a company spokesperson. “If this situation continues, we will face difficulties meeting contractual obligations in both domestic and export markets.”

The government has called for dialogue with protest leaders but has yet to announce concrete measures to ease tensions. Interior Minister Teresa Ríos urged calm and warned against violence: “We recognize the legitimate concerns of citizens, but disruption of vital services puts everyone at risk.”

Analysts warn that prolonged unrest could undermine investor confidence and threaten Chile’s recovery from last year’s recession. “The current instability is reverberating across all sectors,” said Carla Méndez, an economist at Santiago-based consultancy Inversos. “Supply chains are being tested, and the broader impact will depend on how quickly authorities restore order.”

As negotiations continue, unions have signaled that demonstrations will persist until their demands are addressed.
